items.title: 美國上周初領失業金人數小增至20.6萬 就業市場未明顯惡化
items.title_en: U.S. Initial Unemployment Claims Slightly Rise to 206,000 Last Week, Labor Market Not Clearly Deteriorating
paras: 美國上周初領失業救濟金人數小幅增加，但仍處歷史低檔，顯示8月底勞動市場未發生明顯變化，持續呈現企業既不積極招募、也不輕易裁員的「低招募、低裁員」格局。
美國勞工部周四(3日)公布，截至8月29日當周，經季節調整後初領失業救濟金人數增加2,000人至20.6萬人，略高於《路透》調查預估的20.5萬人；前一周數據修正為20.4萬人。平滑短期波動的4周移動平均值小幅升至20萬7,250人。
初領人數目前位於今年18.9萬至23萬人的區間低端，也大致維持在過去一年20萬至23萬人的歷史低檔。企業仍記得新冠疫情封鎖解除後的缺工情況，因此不願輕易裁員；但面對川普政府的貿易及移民政策不確定性，也對增聘員工保持謹慎。
全球人力資源顧問公司Challenger, Gray & Christmas數據顯示，今年前8個月企業宣布的招募計畫較去年同期增加37%，但職缺填補速度似乎不快。8月計畫裁員人數增加58%至5萬2,881人，不過今年迄今宣布的裁員人數仍較去年同期減少41%，低裁員率持續支撐勞動市場與整體經濟。
Fed褐皮書也顯示，8月就業僅「非常小幅」增加，製造業、營建業及部分服務業需求較為健康，零售與餐旅業的勞動需求則呈現下滑。整體招募放緩，使部分失業者需要更長時間才能找到新工作。
截至8月22日當周，續領失業救濟金人數增加8,000人至177.9萬人，但仍低於180萬人。續領人數通常被視為企業招募情況的指標，其上升顯示失業者重返職場的難度略有增加。
市場焦點轉向周五公布的8月非農就業報告。不同調查預估新增就業約5.6萬至6.5萬人，較7月減少2.3萬人回升；失業率估維持4.1%，或小幅升至4.2%。不過，8月就業數據向來容易低於預期，加上海地移民臨時保護身分到期影響工作許可，仍不能排除就業連續第二個月減少。
最新數據顯示，美國勞動市場尚未明顯惡化，可能讓聯準會(Fed)繼續將焦點放在通膨，但招募疲弱也提高進一步收緊政策的風險。市場將密切觀察非農報告，研判Fed本月是否具備升息條件。
paras_en: U.S. initial unemployment benefit claims rose modestly last week but remain at historic lows, indicating that the labor market at the end of August has not changed markedly and continues to exhibit a “low hiring, low layoffs” pattern where firms are neither aggressively recruiting nor readily cutting staff.

The U.S. Labor Department announced on Thursday (the 3rd) that for the week ending August 29, seasonally adjusted initial unemployment claims increased by 2,000 to 206,000, slightly above Reuters’ forecast of 205,000; the prior week’s figure was revised to 204,000. The four‑week moving average, which smooths short‑term volatility, edged up to 207,250.

The current level of initial claims sits at the lower end of this year’s range of 189,000 to 230,000 and roughly within the year‑long historical low band of 200,000 to 230,000. Companies still recall the labor shortages that followed the lifting of COVID‑19 lockdowns and are reluctant to lay off workers, yet uncertainty surrounding the Trump administration’s trade and immigration policies keeps firms cautious about adding staff.

Data from global HR consulting firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas show that corporate hiring plans announced in the first eight months of this year are up 37% from the same period last year, although the speed of filling vacancies appears sluggish. Planned layoffs in August rose 58% to 52,881, but the total layoffs announced so far this year remain 41% lower than a year ago, and the low‑layoff environment continues to support the labor market and the broader economy.

The Fed’s Beige Book also indicated that August employment grew only “very modestly,” with manufacturing, construction and some services showing relatively healthy demand, while labor demand in retail and hospitality declined. Overall hiring slowed, causing some unemployed workers to take longer to find new jobs.

For the week ending August 22, continuing unemployment benefit recipients increased by 8,000 to 1.779 million, still below the 1.8‑million threshold. Continuing claims are often viewed as a gauge of hiring conditions, and their rise suggests a slight increase in the difficulty for the unemployed to re‑enter the workforce.

Market attention now shifts to Friday’s release of the August non‑farm payroll report. Different surveys project an addition of about 56,000 to 65,000 jobs, a rebound of 23,000 from July’s decline; the unemployment rate is expected to hold at 4.1% or edge up to 4.2%. However, August employment data historically tend to fall short of expectations, and the expiration of temporary protected status for some migrant workers could affect work permits, leaving open the possibility of a second consecutive month of job losses.

The latest data suggest that the U.S. labor market has not deteriorated markedly, which may allow the Federal Reserve to keep its focus on inflation, but weak hiring also raises the risk of further policy tightening. Markets will watch the non‑farm payrolls closely to assess whether the Fed has grounds for another rate hike this month.

items.title: 印度被曝要拆換中國通訊設備 帳單30億美元
items.title_en: India Said to Plan Dismantling and Replacing Chinese Telecom Equipment, Cost $3 Billion
paras: 印度政府正在評估潛在「拆除替換」（rip and replace）計畫，考慮以國家安全為由，拆換印度行動通訊網絡中的中國電信設備。
印度財經網站moneycontrol近日援引消息稱，印度政府已向電信公司詳細了解了他們網絡中使用中國設備的情況，比如華為、中興等企業的設備，以及更換這些設備可能產生的成本。
此次摸底工作由印度內政部委托電信部進行，內政部將決定是否啟動拆換計畫。
一位匿名印度官員透露，印度於2021年6月引入「可信來源」機制，要求電信公司必須從獲「可信來源」認證的供應商處採購電信設備，其實就是有了潛在想法。在那前後，印度內政部就一直在評估相關計畫。
印度最大電信公司Reliance Jio沒有部署中國電信設備，但Bharti Airtel、Vodafone Idea以及印度國有電信公司Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited（BSNL）等其他業者，此前都曾在網絡中使用中國廠商的設備。
如果印度最終啟動拆換中國設備的計畫，成本不菲。目前尚不清楚這筆費用將由印度政府承擔，還是由電信公司自行吸收。
印度電信公司本就面臨較大資金壓力。一方面，業者仍在努力將此前投入巨資建設的5G網絡轉化為商業收益；另一方面，他們還需要持續加大光纖網絡建設和通訊基礎設施現代化改造投入。
若印度大規模替換這些設備，電信公司不僅需要重新採購設備，還可能面臨網絡改造、部署和運維等一系列額外成本。業界人士估計，光Airtel和Vodafone兩家業者移除中國通訊硬體和軟體的潛在成本就高達30億美元。
印度並非首個考慮「拆除替換」中國設備的國家。美國已經實施類似計畫，英國、德國、丹麥、愛沙尼亞等歐洲國家也已限制或禁止在5G網絡中使用中國電信設備。
paras_en: India's government is evaluating a potential “rip and replace” plan, considering national‑security grounds to remove Chinese telecom equipment from the country's mobile communications network.

Moneycontrol, an Indian financial website, reported that the government has asked telecom companies for detailed information on the Chinese equipment used in their networks—such as gear from Huawei, ZTE and other firms—and on the possible costs of replacing it.
The fact‑finding effort has been commissioned by the Ministry of Home Affairs to the Ministry of Telecommunications, with the Home Ministry set to decide whether to launch the replacement programme.

An anonymous Indian official disclosed that in June 2021 India introduced a “trusted source” mechanism, requiring telecom operators to procure equipment only from vendors certified as trusted sources, effectively signalling a latent intent. Since then the Home Ministry has been continuously assessing related plans.

India's largest telecom, Reliance Jio, has not deployed Chinese equipment, but other operators—including Bharti Airtel, Vodafone Idea and state‑owned Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL)—have previously used gear from Chinese manufacturers.

If India ultimately initiates the Chinese‑equipment replacement plan, the cost will be substantial. It remains unclear whether the expense will be shouldered by the government or absorbed by the telecom companies themselves.

Indian telecom firms are already under significant financial pressure. On one hand, they are striving to convert the massive investments made in building 5G networks into commercial revenue; on the other, they must continue to pour funds into fiber‑optic network expansion and the modernization of communications infrastructure.

A large‑scale swap would require operators not only to repurchase equipment but also to bear additional expenses for network redesign, deployment and ongoing operations and maintenance. Industry insiders estimate that the potential cost for Airtel and Vodafone alone to remove Chinese hardware and software could reach as high as $3 billion.

India is not the first country to contemplate a “rip and replace” of Chinese equipment. The United States has already implemented a similar programme, and European nations such as the United Kingdom, Germany, Denmark and Estonia have also restricted or banned the use of Chinese telecom gear in their 5G networks.

items.title: 華勒一句話救美債！Fed升息押注降溫 2年期殖利率一度重挫7基點
items.title_en: Waller’s One‑Liner Rescues US Treasuries! Fed Rate‑Hike Bet Cools, 2‑Year Yield Slumps 7 Bps
paras: 美國公債周四(3日)走高，各天期殖利率普遍下跌，聯準會(Fed)理事華勒(Christopher Waller)表示，只要通膨持續降溫，他傾向支持9月維持利率不變，促使交易員下修升息押注，美元兌10國集團(G10)貨幣全面走弱。
美債殖利率全線下跌3至5個基點，其中對Fed政策較敏感的2年期殖利率領跌，一度重挫7個基點至4.30%。市場先前預期Fed本月可能升息，2年期殖利率本周一度突破4.40%，為2025年1月以來首見。美元則一度下跌0.5%。
Mischler Financial Group董事總經理Tom di Galoma表示，華勒談話讓美債市場「鬆了一口氣」，顯示他在更多通膨數據出爐前，仍屬於主張按兵不動的陣營。
華勒表示，如果通膨持續朝Fed的2%目標邁進，他願意支持將政策利率維持在目前水準。美國通膨率已由5月的4.1%降至7月的3.7%，儘管仍高於目標，近期下降趨勢已讓他更願意保持耐心。
華勒過去一年的政策立場多次轉變。他在2025年7月及2026年1月曾反對維持利率不變，主張降息；今年5月22日及7月13日則轉向偏鷹，當時的發言均曾推升美債殖利率。
利率交換市場目前僅反映9月升息1碼約一半的可能性，並預估Fed年底前累計升息約33個基點。本周稍早，由於油價上漲可能阻礙通膨降溫，市場一度反映9月升息18個基點、年底前累計升息41個基點。
市場下一步將關注周五(4日)公布的8月非農就業報告。《彭博》調查預估，美國8月非農就業人數增加5.5萬人，扭轉7月意外下滑的局面。若數據表現疲弱，美債可能進一步走高，但漲幅恐受到債券供給增加的壓力限制。
美國市場在周一勞動節假期後恢復交易時，財政部將標售3年期、10年期及30年期公債，企業發債活動也可望回升。市場策略師警告，即使未來數據支持Fed保持觀望，央行若不採取行動，仍可能再度引發外界對其抗通膨信譽的質疑。
paras_en: US Treasury yields rose on Thursday, with yields across all maturities falling. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said that as long as inflation keeps cooling, he leans toward keeping rates unchanged in September, prompting traders to cut their rate‑hike bets and the dollar to weaken against all G10 currencies.

All Treasury yields slipped 3‑5 basis points, with the 2‑year yield—most sensitive to Fed policy—leading the decline, at one point plunging 7 basis points to 4.30%. The market had previously expected a possible Fed hike this month, sending the 2‑year yield above 4.40% earlier in the week, a level not seen since January 2025. The dollar also fell about 0.5% at one point.

Tom di Galoma, Managing Director at Mischler Financial Group, said Waller’s comments gave the Treasury market “a sigh of relief,” indicating that he remains in the camp favoring a wait‑and‑see approach until more inflation data arrive.

Waller said that if inflation continues moving toward the Fed’s 2% target, he is willing to support keeping the policy rate at its current level. US inflation has fallen from 4.1% in May to 3.7% in July, still above target but the recent downward trend makes him more patient.

Waller’s policy stance has shifted several times over the past year. He opposed keeping rates steady and advocated cuts in July 2025 and January 2026, while in May 22 and July 13 this year he turned more hawkish, with those remarks previously pushing Treasury yields higher.

The interest‑rate swap market now reflects roughly a 50% chance of a one‑tick (0.25 percentage‑point) hike in September and projects about 33 basis points of cumulative hikes by year‑end. Earlier this week, concerns that rising oil prices could stall inflation cooling led the market to price in an 18‑basis‑point hike in September and a 41‑basis‑point cumulative increase by year‑end.

The market’s next focus will be the August non‑farm payroll report due on Friday, September 4. Bloomberg’s poll estimates US non‑farm employment will rise by 55,000 jobs, reversing July’s unexpected decline. If the data come in weak, Treasury yields could rise further, though the upside may be capped by increased bond supply.

When US markets resumed trading after the Labor Day holiday on Monday, the Treasury Department will auction 3‑year, 10‑year and 30‑year bonds, and corporate issuance is expected to pick up. Market strategists warn that even if future data support a Fed hold, inaction by the central bank could again spark doubts about its credibility in fighting inflation.

items.title_en: TWD Decouples from Asian Currencies! Stocks and FX Both Fall, Volume Shrinks, Two Consecutive Red Days, Close at 31.755
paras: 台北股匯今(3)日走勢震盪，台股尾盤賣壓出籠收黑，新台幣兌美元先升後貶，一度摜破 31.8 元關卡，並未跟隨日元等亞幣走強，在央行出手調節下，終場貶勢收斂，收在 31.755 元，貶值 2.7 分，為連 2 黑，台北與元太外匯市場總成交值萎縮至 27.31 億美元。
新台幣兌美元今天開盤價為 31.75 元，早盤最高升抵 31.70 元，但隨著熱錢流出，匯價最低來到 31.827 元，所幸尾盤靠央行介入穩匯，驚險收復 31.8 元關卡，以 31.755 元作收，貶值 2.7 分。
美伊緊張局勢升溫，再度掀起升息疑慮，台股今天尾盤急殺 307 點，失守46000點關卡，收在 45857.66 點，台積電、聯發科表現有撐，但記憶體、PCB 等電子族群賣壓沉重。三大法人合計賣超637.11億元，其中外資及陸資賣超481.46億元。
觀察主要亞幣今天對美元表現，日元強勢大漲 1.62%，韓元同步勁揚0.66%，星幣升值 0.33%，人民幣升值 0.06%，新台幣走勢獨憔悴，收盤下挫 0.09%。
日元日前一度貶破 160 兌 1 美元大關，隨後於 2 日急升至 158 字頭。隨著美國財長貝森特(Scott Bessent)近期公開敦促日本升息，市場人士解讀，160 關卡可能已成為美方與日本央行(BOJ)共同防守的新底線。日銀將於 9 月 17 日至 18 日召開貨幣政策會議，總裁植田和男面臨進退兩難局面，而市場目前已高度反映本月升息 1 碼的預期。
paras_en: Taipei's stock and FX markets were volatile today (the 3rd), with the Taiwan index ending the session in the red under selling pressure. The New Taiwan dollar rose against the US dollar before falling, briefly breaking the 31.8 level, and did not follow the rally in the yen and other Asian currencies. After the central bank intervened, the depreciation eased and the dollar closed at 31.755, down 2.7 cents, marking a second consecutive red day. Total turnover in the Taipei and Yuan‑Tai foreign‑exchange markets shrank to $2.731 billion.

The New Taiwan dollar opened at 31.75 per US dollar, climbed to a high of 31.70 in early trading, but as hot money fled, the rate fell to a low of 31.827. Fortunately, central‑bank intervention near the close steadied the market, narrowly reclaiming the 31.8 barrier and finishing at 31.755, down 2.7 cents.

Rising US‑Iran tensions revived rate‑hike concerns, and the Taiwan index plunged 307 points in the final session, slipping below the 46,000 mark to close at 45,857.66. TSMC and MediaTek provided some support, but memory‑chip, PCB and other electronics sectors faced heavy selling. The three major institutional investors sold a combined NT$63.711 billion, with foreign and mainland investors accounting for NT$48.146 billion of the net outflow.

Looking at the performance of major Asian currencies against the dollar, the yen surged 1.62%, the won rose 0.66%, the Singapore dollar appreciated 0.33%, the renminbi gained 0.06%, while the New Taiwan dollar was the only one to weaken, closing down 0.09%.

The yen had briefly slipped past the 160 per dollar threshold before rallying sharply to the 158 range on the 2nd. After US Treasury official Scott Bessent publicly urged Japan to raise rates, market participants read that the 160 level may now serve as a new joint floor defended by the US and the Bank of Japan. The BOJ is set to hold its monetary policy meeting on September 17‑18, with Governor Kazuo Ueda facing a dilemma, and markets have already priced in a one‑percentage‑point rate hike this month.

items.title: 日元飛速飆升 日銀本次並未大規模干預 空軍畏戰主動平倉
items.title_en: Yen Soars Rapidly; BOJ Does Not Intervene on a Large Scale; Traders Fear Intervention and Close Shorts
paras: 日元兌美元匯率周三(2日)與周四出現強烈波動，走勢自 160.38 快速升值並突破 158 關卡，盤中甚至一度創下近一個月新高 156.36。這波急劇漲勢迅速引發市場熱議，猜測日本政府是否再度出手干預匯市。
然而，日本央行(BOJ)公布的經常帳數據顯示，本周並無大規模干預的跡象。市場分析指出，此波行情並非官方直接干預，而是由交易員對央行升息預期的「重新定價」以及對干預的畏懼心理所驅動。
根據日本央行的預測，其經常帳因財政因素預計減少 4,100 億日元，與貨幣經紀商估計的 7,000 億日元差距不大，遠低於 2022 年以來日本最小干預規模的 7,290 億日元，證實日本官方並未入市。
儘管如此，上月底美日聯手斥資 15.4 兆日元的歷史性干預，已徹底改變了交易員的心理防線。當日元兌美元再度逼近 160 大關時，畏懼干預的心理促使大量日元空頭部位在官方實際行動前便主動平倉。
更為關鍵且持久的支撐力道，來自於市場對日本央行貨幣政策升息路徑的重新定價。日本央行政策委員高田創日前發表鷹派演說，明確指出「2026年是貨幣政策的體制轉變」，並強調升息應是「敏捷且依據數據的」，不應受限於市場預期的固定間隔。
此發言直接挑戰了過往每半年調整一次的市場假設。目前隔夜指數交換(OIS)定價顯示，市場預期未來 12 個月將累計升息約 96.5 個基點，且 9 月升息的機率高達 84%。
此外，美國財政部長貝森特對日本政策正常化表達強烈支持，美日政策立場趨於一致，進一步削弱了市場放任日元過度貶值的信心。
paras_en: The yen‑dollar exchange rate experienced sharp volatility on Wednesday (the 2nd) and Thursday, climbing quickly from 160.38 and breaking through the 158 level, even touching a near‑one‑month high of 156.36 intraday. This rapid surge sparked heated market debate about whether the Japanese government would intervene in the FX market again.

However, the current‑account data released by the Bank of Japan (BOJ) showed no signs of large‑scale intervention this week. Analysts note that the move was not driven by direct official action but by traders re‑pricing expectations of BOJ rate hikes and a fear‑based mindset regarding possible intervention.

According to BOJ forecasts, the current account is expected to shrink by ¥410 billion due to fiscal factors, a figure close to the ¥700 billion estimate from currency dealers and far below the smallest intervention since 2022 of ¥729 billion, confirming that officials have not entered the market.

Nevertheless, the historic joint US‑Japan intervention at the end of last month, worth ¥15.4 trillion, has fundamentally altered traders’ psychological defenses. When the yen‑dollar pair again approached the 160 threshold, the fear of intervention prompted many short yen positions to be closed voluntarily before any official action materialised.

A more critical and lasting source of support comes from the market’s re‑pricing of the BOJ’s monetary‑policy tightening path. BOJ policy board member Hiroshi Takata recently delivered a hawkish speech, stating clearly that “2026 will be a structural shift in monetary policy,” and emphasizing that rate hikes should be “agile and data‑driven,” not constrained by fixed intervals dictated by market expectations.

His remarks directly challenge the long‑standing assumption of semi‑annual rate adjustments. Current overnight index swap (OIS) pricing indicates the market expects roughly 96.5 basis points of hikes over the next 12 months, with an 84% probability of a rate increase in September.

In addition, U.S. Treasury Secretary Vincent expressed strong support for Japan’s policy normalization, aligning U.S. and Japanese stances and further eroding market confidence in allowing the yen to depreciate excessively.

items.title: 全球機構投資人美元避險比率降至歷史新低 美元潛在拋售壓力巨大
items.title_en: Global Institutional Investors' Dollar Hedging Ratio Falls to Historic Low, Creating Massive Potential Dollar Sell Pressure
paras: 根據全球退休基金與保險公司最新申報資料，一些最龐大的美國資產持有者對美元走弱，幾乎沒有提供任何保護，這使得美元一旦面臨市場情緒逆轉，將面臨更急劇下跌的風險。
在包括日本、加拿大與台灣等六個主要市場中，截至今年6月30日，這些投資人對其外幣曝險僅進行了41%的避險，創下2015年以來的最低紀錄。這反映出隨著美元逐漸穩定，去年因川普政府關稅政策而急於規避美元損失的熱潮已然退去。

微幅調整避險比率 將引發數千億美元流動

Nuveen宏觀信用主管 Laura Cooper 表示：「鑑於外資持有美國資產的龐大規模，即便只是微幅調整避險比率，都可能引發顯著的外匯資金流動。」
根據彭博計算，這六個主要市場(還包含澳洲、丹麥與芬蘭)的外幣持有規模達4.6兆美元，避險比率只要提高5個百分點，就相當於高達2,300億美元的本國貨幣交易量。
Manulife投資管理多元資產方案投資長 Nathan Thooft 分析，若市場持續排除聯準會升息的可能性，且利差進一步收窄，投資人可能會開始重新建立避險部位，這將成為美元持續面臨賣壓的固定來源。

專家建議多元化資產配置

過去投資人減少避險是因為避險成本高昂，且相信美元在市場動盪時能發揮避險作用，藉此沖抵美國股債換回本國貨幣時的損失。然而，QIC多元資產方案主管 Stuart Simmons 警告，在政經不確定性升溫的時代，若仍過度依賴美元作為防禦手段，可能不再管用，他建議投資人應重新檢視並在海外資產組合中納入更多元的配置。
Equiti集團首席市場策略師 Noureldeen AlHammoury 指出，如果投資人不再確信美元能在市場恐慌時可靠地升值，就沒有理由繼續容忍龐大的未避險外幣曝險。
他補充說明，投資人並不需要拋售美股或美債，只需透過遠期外匯市場拋售美元來進行避險，這代表即使美國資產需求維持強勁，美元本身仍將面臨下行壓力。

日本可能成為集體避險的領頭羊

此波潛在的避險潮在亞洲及歐洲地區尤為關鍵。日本作為全球最大的美國公債海外持有國，避險需求可能最為迫切。
德意志銀行日本首席固定收益策略師Shoki Omori 表示，上一次避險比率如此低的時期是在2013年，當時美元正要開啟長達十年的多頭市場，而如今的總體經濟環境更像是當年的鏡像。
他預期，日本央行進一步升息收窄利差、美元急貶或壽險業新清償能力制度的推行，都可能成為觸發集體避險的催化劑。
paras_en: According to the latest filings from global pension funds and insurance companies, some of the largest holders of U.S. assets provide virtually no protection against a weakening dollar, meaning that if market sentiment reverses, the dollar could face a sharply accelerated decline.

Across six major markets—including Japan, Canada and Taiwan—by June 30 of this year these investors had hedged only 41% of their foreign‑currency exposure, the lowest level since 2015. This reflects that as the dollar has steadied, the rush last year to avoid dollar losses driven by the Trump administration’s tariff policies has faded.

A modest adjustment to the hedging ratio could trigger tens of billions of dollars of liquidity flows, says Laura Cooper, head of macro credit at Nuveen. "Given the massive scale of foreign holdings of U.S. assets, even a slight tweak in hedging ratios can generate significant foreign‑exchange capital movements," she said.

Bloomberg estimates that the foreign‑currency holdings in these six key markets (which also include Australia, Denmark and Finland) total $4.6 trillion. Raising the hedging ratio by just five percentage points would correspond to about $230 billion of domestic‑currency transactions.

Nathan Thooft, head of multi‑asset solutions at Manulife Investment Management, analyses that if markets continue to rule out further Fed rate hikes and yield spreads narrow further, investors may start rebuilding hedges, providing a persistent source of dollar‑selling pressure.

Experts advise diversifying asset allocations. In the past, investors reduced hedging because of high costs and the belief that the dollar would act as a safe haven during market turmoil, offsetting losses when U.S. equities and bonds were converted back to local currency. However, Stuart Simmons, head of multi‑asset solutions at QIC, warns that in an era of rising geopolitical uncertainty, over‑reliance on the dollar as a defensive tool may no longer work and recommends reassessing portfolios to include more diversified overseas allocations.

Equiti Group chief market strategist Noureldeen AlHammoury notes that if investors no longer trust the dollar to reliably appreciate during market panic, there is no reason to tolerate large un‑hedged foreign‑currency exposures.

He adds that investors do not need to sell U.S. stocks or bonds; they can hedge by selling dollars in the forward‑FX market, meaning that even if demand for U.S. assets stays strong, the dollar itself would still face downward pressure.

Japan could emerge as the leader of a collective hedging wave. This potential hedging surge is especially critical in Asia and Europe, and Japan, as the world’s largest foreign holder of U.S. Treasury bonds, may have the most urgent hedging needs.

Shoki Omori, chief fixed‑income strategist for Japan at Deutsche Bank, says the last time hedging ratios were this low was in 2013, when the dollar was about to embark on a decade‑long bull market, and today’s macro environment resembles a mirror image of that period.

He expects that further rate hikes by the Bank of Japan narrowing spreads, a rapid dollar depreciation, or the rollout of new solvency‑based regulations for life insurers could all act as catalysts triggering a collective hedging response.

items.title_en: US Bonds Raise Alarm! Overseas US Asset Hedging Ratio Hits Ten-Year Low; Experts Say Depreciation Trades Are Heating Up, and a Dollar Collapse Could Trigger Continuous Liquidations
paras: 外媒最新報導出，根據日本、加拿大、台灣、澳洲、丹麥及芬蘭等六地退休基金與保險公司申報文件，截至今年6月30日，海外投資人持有美股美債的外幣曝險避險比率僅約41%，創2015年來新低。
去年川普推出全球關稅、美元急貶時，上述避險比率曾短暫跳升，但這股熱潮隨著美元回穩、避險成本居高不下而迅速消退，投資人重回「波動時美元自動避險」的舊策略，也就是靠美元升值緩衝本幣計價的美國資產回撤，省下昂貴的衍生品費用。
但美元本季跌約2%、兌多數G10貨幣走弱，「貶值交易」(debasement trade)重新升溫，加上美日聯手干預日元、美國財政部擴大長債回購來壓抑殖利率，加上市場質疑聯準會(Fed)主席華許會否真升息抗通膨，均加劇「美國政策侵蝕美元」的敘事。
匯率避險是利用衍生性商品賣出美元、買進投資人本國貨幣，以防範匯率波動。由於美國資產在全球投資組合中佔有很大比重，增加避險其實意味著更多美元賣盤。
管理1.4兆美元的Nuveen宏觀信貸主管Laura Coope指出，海外持美資產規模龐大，避險比率只需小幅上調，就能撬動可觀外匯流量。根據測算，上述六地合計4.6兆美元外幣部位中，避險比率每上升5個百分點，等於約2300億美元交易量。
雖然上述估算未納入英國和歐元區等主要市場，但所涵蓋國家仍占美國資產海外持有量相當大的一部分。日本是全球最大的美國國債海外持有國，佔外國持有量約10%，加拿大和台灣也高居前十名。
paras_en: Foreign media reports that, based on filing documents from pension funds and insurance companies in Japan, Canada, Taiwan, Australia, Denmark and Finland, the foreign‑currency hedging ratio for overseas investors’ US equity and US Treasury holdings was only about 41% as of June 30 this year, a new low not seen since 2015.

Last year, when President Trump rolled out global tariffs and the dollar sharply depreciated, the hedging ratio briefly spiked, but the rally faded quickly as the dollar steadied and hedging costs remained high. Investors reverted to the old “automatic dollar hedge in volatile times” approach—relying on a stronger dollar to cushion the pull‑back of US‑denominated assets priced in local currencies and saving on expensive derivatives fees.

However, the dollar has fallen roughly 2% this quarter and weakened against most G10 currencies, reviving “debasement trades.” Combined with coordinated US‑Japan intervention in the yen, the US Treasury’s expanded long‑bond buybacks to suppress yields, and market doubts about whether Fed Chair Jerome Powell will truly raise rates to combat inflation, the narrative that “US policy is eroding the dollar” has intensified.

Currency hedging uses derivatives to sell dollars and buy the investor’s home currency to guard against exchange‑rate swings. Because US assets make up a large share of global portfolios, increasing hedges actually means more dollar selling pressure.

Laura Coope, head of macro credit at Nuveen, which manages $1.4 trillion, notes that overseas holdings of US assets are massive, and a modest uptick in the hedging ratio could mobilise a sizable FX flow. Her calculations show that among the six jurisdictions, the combined $4.6 trillion foreign‑currency exposure would generate about $230 billion of transaction volume for each 5‑percentage‑point rise in the hedging ratio.

Although the estimate excludes major markets such as the UK and the euro‑area, the covered countries still represent a substantial share of overseas US‑asset holdings. Japan is the world’s largest foreign holder of US Treasury bonds, accounting for roughly 10% of foreign holdings, with Canada and Taiwan also ranking among the top ten.

In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, fell 0.1% to 99.60. The index had risen 0.3% on Tuesday.

The wave of selling in sovereign bonds eased on Wednesday, prompting traders to turn back to equities. U.S. Treasury yields and other major 10‑year sovereign yields had hit multi‑year highs on Tuesday. The 10‑year U.S. yield rose to its highest level since November 2023, while the 2‑year yield reached a new peak not seen since July 2024.

Bond sell‑offs were driven by several factors, including inflation worries from persistently high oil prices, concerns over debt sustainability as companies borrow heavily to build AI infrastructure, and the continual expansion of fiscal deficits worldwide. Higher yields raise borrowing costs, which can pressure consumers and businesses, and a higher‑rate environment generally supports a stronger dollar.
On Wednesday the U.S. yield curve steadied, with the 10‑year Treasury slipping 1.2 basis points to 4.784% and the 2‑year falling 2.1 basis points to 4.373%.
Ahead of the much‑watched August non‑farm payroll report due on Friday, the market also received additional U.S. economic and labor‑market data.

ADP data showed private‑sector employers added 38,000 jobs in August, well below the 47,000 forecast and the slowest growth since January this year. However, strong U.S. manufacturing data offset the weak ADP numbers. July manufacturing new orders rose 0.9% month‑over‑month to $663.6 billion, beating the 0.7% estimate.

In addition, the Federal Reserve’s latest Beige Book indicated that economic activity has grown modestly across the United States since early July, with 10 of the 12 Fed districts reporting growth ranging from slight to moderate.
Oil prices continued to rise, though the gains were smaller than on Tuesday. Brent crude futures for November delivery were up 0.6% at $95.26 a barrel, after a 4.6% jump the previous session.

U.S.–Iran tensions rose to their highest level in weeks, with military attacks intensifying again. The U.S. Central Command said on Tuesday it had completed a new round of strikes against targets of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, including air‑defense installations, radar systems and communications facilities.
Canadian dollar strengthens as Bank of Canada holds rates steady

The loonie rose 0.4% on Wednesday. Earlier, the Bank of Canada announced it would keep its policy rate unchanged but warned that inflation risks have risen and that the trade dispute with the United States adds uncertainty to the economic outlook.

Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem noted that, since the July rate decision, the Middle‑East conflict still shows no sign of resolution. He also stressed that new U.S. tariffs could pose a risk to an economic rebound, but he expects the tariffs will not have a major direct impact on overall economic activity.
The New Zealand dollar fell more than 0.7% against the U.S. dollar, marking its worst single‑day performance since June 23.

The kiwi’s weakness stemmed from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand’s policy decision. While officials raised the cash rate by 25 basis points, they simultaneously issued an unexpectedly dovish forward guidance.
Japanese yen rebounds from 160 level as BOJ readies rate‑hike discussion

The yen strengthened against the dollar, climbing back above the key 160 threshold. Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda earlier confirmed at a news conference that the central bank will discuss a rate hike in September, focusing on whether energy‑price‑driven inflation pressures threaten medium‑term price stability.
BOJ board member Hajime Takata further reinforced hawkish market expectations, advocating a more flexible path for future rate increases.
Just a day earlier, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, speaking at a G20 meeting in North Carolina, urged Japanese officials to take “decisive” action to address the yen’s persistent weakness.

items.title_en: US and Japan Act Again? Yen Falls Below 160 Then Suddenly Surges, Sparking Intervention Rumors
paras: 日元周三(2日)盤中突然快速升值，在20國集團(G20)會議即將落幕之際，引發日本與美國可能再次進場干預匯市的揣測。由於當時沒有明顯新聞或總體經濟因素足以解釋這波走勢，市場交易室隨即傳出官方出手買進日元的說法。
日元稍早一度貶破160日元兌1美元，隨後突然急速反彈，但漲勢並未持續擴大。市場人士認為，160日元可能已成為美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)與日本銀行(BOJ)共同防守的新底線。
美國銀行(BAC-US)外匯策略師Alex Cohen表示，市場仍對匯市干預保持高度警戒。部分交易員則認為，這波升勢可能只是市場掃除停損單，也就是日元貶破關鍵價位後，引發大量部位自動平倉；不過，仍不能排除相關走勢是由官方力量觸發。
Monex外匯交易員Andrew Hazlett表示，市場確實傳出官方干預的消息，但就本次波動幅度而言，他對這項說法持懷疑態度。然而，日元兌美元與歐元同時突然走強，也很難以其他原因解釋。
這次日元升幅仍小於約一個月前的行情。當時日元一度貶至約164日元兌1美元，創近40年低點，隨後東京與華府聯手進場支撐日元，推動日元反彈約5%。
那是美日自1998年以來首次協調買進日元，也是數十年來罕見的聯合匯市干預。兩國政府事後均暗示，如有必要不排除再次採取共同行動，大幅提高做空日元的風險。隨著160日元關卡再度失守，交易員正密切觀察官方是否已悄然出手，或準備進行新一輪干預。
paras_en: The yen suddenly surged mid‑session on Wednesday (the 2nd), just as the G20 summit was winding down, prompting speculation that Japan and the United States might intervene in the currency market again. Because there was no obvious news or macro‑economic factor to explain the move, market desks quickly began circulating rumors that officials were buying yen.

Earlier the yen had slipped past the ¥160 per US$1 mark, then abruptly rebounded, though the rally did not continue to expand. Market participants think the ¥160 level may have become a new defensive floor jointly defended by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and the Bank of Japan.

Bank of America (BAC-US) FX strategist Alex Cohen said the market remains on high alert for currency‑market intervention. Some traders believe the rise may simply be a market‑wide stop‑loss sweep—positions automatically liquidated after the yen broke a key level—but they do not rule out that the move was triggered by official forces.

Monex FX trader Andrew Hazlett noted that rumors of official intervention are indeed circulating, but given the modest size of this move he is skeptical of that claim. Still, the simultaneous strength of the yen against both the dollar and the euro is hard to explain by any other reason.

The current yen gain is smaller than the move about a month ago, when the yen briefly fell to around ¥164 per US$1, a near‑40‑year low, before Tokyo and Washington jointly stepped in to support it, pushing the yen up roughly 5%.

That episode marked the first coordinated yen‑buying by the United States and Japan since 1998 and was a rare joint intervention in decades. Both governments later hinted that, if necessary, they would not rule out another coordinated action, dramatically raising the risk of shorting the yen. With the ¥160 barrier breached again, traders are watching closely to see whether officials have already acted quietly or are preparing a new round of intervention.

items.title: 貝森特把日銀逼入死局！升息1碼怕市場不買單 不升日元恐再崩
items.title_en: Bessent Forces BOJ into a Deadlock! Raising Rates by One Point Risks Market Rejection; Not Raising Yen May Cause Further Collapse
paras: 日本銀行(BOJ)將於9月17日至18日召開政策會議，總裁植田和男正陷入罕見的進退兩難局面。美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)近期公開敦促日本升息，市場也已完全反映本月升息1碼的預期；然而，日銀無論升息或按兵不動，都可能引發金融市場劇烈波動。
日銀目前政策利率為1%。期貨與交換市場顯示，投資人已完全反映本月升息1碼至1.25%的可能性。若日銀按兵不動，不僅將讓市場大感意外，也可能導致日元重挫，進一步推升進口成本與通膨。市場預估，日本通膨率今年稍後可能接近3%。
然而，僅升息1碼(25個基點)也未必足以穩定市場。日銀審議委員高田創周三(2日)提出可能採取更大幅度行動的構想，並暗示不排除連續升息，使一般幅度的升息可能更難滿足投資人期待。
摩根大通證券首席日本經濟學家Ayako Fujita表示，美方已將話說到這種程度，日銀若不採取行動恐怕會引發問題；但如果市場認為日銀只能在美國支持下升息，也可能損害政策效果及央行公信力。

日元與日債市場同陷不安

日本債市近期持續遭到拋售，10年期公債殖利率周二突破3%，為1996年以來首見；同期間，美國10年期公債殖利率逼近4.82%，升至貝森特上任前以來最高水準。
貝森特自去年起便多次敦促日銀收緊貨幣政策，主要擔心日本公債市場動盪外溢至美國。日元貶值也可能迫使日本出售持有的美債以進行匯市干預，進而加重美債賣壓並推升美國借貸成本。
樂天證券經濟研究所首席經濟學家、前日銀官員Nobuyasu Atago指出，貝森特之所以敦促日銀升息，是因為他相信此舉有助抑制全球公債殖利率上升，最終也將使美國受惠。
貝森特近日透過社群貼文、媒體訪問及會談持續向日本施壓，要求日銀「做正確的事」，並敦促東京結束再通膨政策。他本周在美國北卡羅來納州舉行的G20會議期間與植田和男會面，雙方討論如何透過健全的政策制定穩定通膨預期，並避免匯率過度波動。

不升息恐讓匯市干預成果付諸流水

植田和男至今未釋出日銀可能將行動延後至10月的訊號。他在G20會議後表示，政策委員會將把物價上行風險納入決策考量，被市場解讀為暗示9月可能升息。高田創隨後更提出連續升息的可能性；日銀最近一次升息是在6月，與前一次行動相隔6個月。
若日銀在市場已完全押注升息的情況下按兵不動，日元可能再度重挫，也可能招致貝森特強烈反應。美日7月31日罕見聯手買進日元，為1998年以來首次共同干預匯市，一度使日元從1986年來低點、約164日元兌1美元，回升至接近155日元。日元周三在紐約市場約報158.72日元，交易員仍警戒美日再次出手干預。
Marlborough Investment Management基金經理James Athey表示，日銀必須升息並發出更強硬訊號，否則先前支撐日元的努力可能付諸流水。他認為，日銀7月未在匯市干預與政治表態已經鋪路的情況下升息，是一項重大錯誤。
不過，分析師認為，日本長期殖利率上升的核心原因並非日銀政策，而是市場對政府財政赤字的疑慮。若日本政府無法提出可信的財政方針，即使日銀升息，也未必能同時阻止日元走弱與長期公債殖利率攀升。
paras_en: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) will hold its policy meeting on September 17‑18, putting President Kazuo Ueda in a rare dilemma. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has recently urged Japan to raise rates, and markets have fully priced in a one‑point hike this month; however, whether the BOJ hikes or stays put could trigger sharp market turbulence.

The BOJ’s policy rate stands at 1%. Futures and swap markets show investors have fully priced in a one‑point rise to 1.25% this month. If the BOJ stays idle, it will not only surprise the market but could also cause the yen to slump, further raising import costs and inflation. Markets estimate Japan’s inflation rate may approach 3% later this year.

Yet, a single one‑point (25 basis points) hike may not stabilize the market. BOJ policy committee member Takada Sō announced on Wednesday (2) that a larger move might be considered, hinting that consecutive hikes are not ruled out, making a modest increase harder to satisfy investors’ expectations.

Morgan Stanley Securities chief Japanese economist Ayako Fujita said the U.S. has pushed the issue to this extent; if the BOJ does nothing, problems may arise. However, if the market believes the BOJ can only hike with U.S. support, it could damage policy effectiveness and central bank credibility.

The yen and Japanese bond market are both uneasy. Japan’s bond market has been under selling pressure, with the 10‑year yield breaking 3% on Tuesday for the first time since 1996; meanwhile, the U.S. 10‑year yield approached 4.82%, rising to its highest level since Bessent took office.

Since last year, Bessent has repeatedly urged the BOJ to tighten policy, mainly worried that volatility in Japan’s bond market could spill over to the U.S. A weaker yen could force Japan to sell its U.S. bonds to intervene in the FX market, further increasing selling pressure on U.S. bonds and raising U.S. borrowing costs.
Lotte Securities’ chief economist and former BOJ official Nobuyasu Atago said Bessent’s push for a hike stems from his belief that it will curb global bond yields, ultimately benefiting the U.S.

Bessent has recently used social media posts, media interviews, and talks to pressure Japan, urging the BOJ to "do the right thing" and push Tokyo to end its inflation policy. This week, during the G20 meeting in North Carolina, he met Ueda and discussed how sound policy could stabilize inflation expectations and avoid excessive currency volatility.

Ueda has not yet signaled that the BOJ might delay action until October. After the G20 meeting, he said the policy committee would incorporate price‑upward risk into decisions, which the market interpreted as a hint of a September hike. Takada Sō then suggested the possibility of consecutive hikes; the BOJ’s last hike was in June, six months after the previous one.

If the BOJ remains idle while markets have fully bet on a hike, the yen could slump again and provoke a strong reaction from Bessent. On July 31, the U.S. and Japan jointly bought yen—a rare move since 1998—temporarily lifting the yen from its low of about 164 per dollar to nearly 155. On Wednesday, the yen traded around 158.72 in New York, with traders wary of another intervention.

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough Investment Management, said the BOJ must hike and send a stronger signal, otherwise previous efforts to support the yen could be wasted. He believes the BOJ’s July decision not to intervene in the FX market and make a political statement was a major mistake.

However, analysts say the core reason for rising long‑term yields in Japan is not BOJ policy but market concerns over government fiscal deficits. If the Japanese government cannot present a credible fiscal plan, even a BOJ hike may not simultaneously stop the yen from weakening and long‑term bond yields from climbing.
